entries.threshold_tripped: days since last retro > 7 (no retro has ever been recorded; learnings.json untouched since 2026-09-18, 22 days)
entries.authorised_by: Caleb, explicitly, when presented with the block and the alternatives
entries.note: Bypass accepted silently per the rule's abuse-detection ladder (0 prior bypasses in 30 days). Recorded so the NEXT bypass is the warned one rather than starting the count over. The substance of the block stands and is not resolved by this entry: roughly eight durable learnings from the 2026-09-22..2026-10-03 work exist only in the assistant's own memory (two-surfaces-check, measure-before-picking-a-threshold, pipefail-early-quit-consumer, activity-is-not-abandonment, qa-duplicate-dispatch-not-merge-race, comments-asserting-all-callers, qa-brief-assert-sha-not-version, gitea-actions-api-logs) and NOT in this file. The project's knowledge base being empty is an accurate record of that gap, not a reporting error.

entries.title: The QA pool is reachable only by NATS dispatch through Joe
entries.body: ada/gracie consume friend.qa.task.> off NATS only. A Gitea reviewer request never reaches them, so a PR awaiting 'review' that was never dispatched waits forever. Route briefs through joe_tmux_1.

entries.title: No token here can self-approve, and ci-docs-approver cannot merge
entries.body: Every token authenticates as finish06, and Gitea refuses self-approval, so a PR author can never satisfy main's one-approval gate. Separately, ci-docs-approver holds review-only rights: it approves and then the merge API returns 405. A docs PR can therefore sit green AND approved with nobody noticing, and the cause is not a missing approval. Observed on #499.

entries.title: The 'merge race' was a misdiagnosis; the defect is duplicate QA dispatch
entries.body: Measured across the 28 most recent merged PRs: 25 merged within 60s of approval (median ~5s), so the interval the complaint named is 89% of all merges and not a signal. The real defect is that both ada and gracie work the same PR (10/28) with no claim on the task, and the loser's findings land after the merge (7/28). Critically, a reviews-only query UNDERCOUNTS this by exactly the cases that matter: Gitea refuses a review event on a merged PR, so the losing reviewer posts an issue comment, invisible to /pulls/{n}/reviews (4 of the 10). Any check of whether the fix worked must union reviews AND comments. Fix dispatched: lease friend.qa.task.<pr>.

entries.title: Reading Gitea Actions results over the API
entries.body: The id in actions/tasks is NOT the run id — /actions/runs/{that_id} 404s; the run id is the last path segment of the object's own url. Job logs live only at actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs. The tasks response carries total_count; a limit is a page size, not a total. And a job log contains the script TEXT as well as its output, so grepping for an echo string matches twice on success and once where it never executed — anchor on the timestamp prefix that only real output carries.

entries.title: Where two surfaces state one fact, checking one proves nothing about the other
entries.body: Every defect shipped in this window passed a check that looked at something adjacent and correct: the footer version badge was right while the changelog overlay was two releases stale; showUptimeDisplay persisted perfectly and gated an element that is display:none at the default density. It applies to TESTS too — code-splitting.test.ts greps src/ for lazy(() => import()) and stayed green at 2 passed while manualChunks folded every overlay into the entry chunk and the initial download grew 98.8 -> 108.2 kB. Check the surface the user sees, in the built artifact.

entries.title: A threshold picked by feel is wrong in an unpredictable direction
entries.body: ENTRY_JS_GZIP_BUDGET was set to 115,000 against a 98,849 B baseline by feel (~16%). Building every 16.x tag gave worst single-release growth +2,056 B and a median ~+490 B, so that was ~8 releases of headroom at the worst rate and ~33 at the median. Then the SAME mistake in the other direction: the CSS budget was set to 19,500 by analogy to the JS percentage rather than measured — only 1.7x the worst observed CSS release, which ordinary token work would have breached. Build the historical series first, pick a multiple of the worst observed delta, and write the series into the file.

entries.title: Under pipefail, never pipe into a consumer that quits early
entries.body: mr-staging and staging-release ran `curl ... | sed '/^---$/q' | kubectl apply -f -`. sed quits at the first ---, closing the pipe while curl is still writing; curl exits 23 (CURLE_WRITE_ERROR) and pipefail promotes it, so the job failed AFTER kubectl apply had already succeeded. Reproduced 25/25; the download-then-extract form 0/40. Two further lessons: pipefail can be INVISIBLE (the composite declared plain `shell: bash` and Gitea expands it to `bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail`), and a red deploy does NOT mean nothing changed — the ConfigMap was live in staging while the status was red.

entries.title: Measuring activity cannot conclude abandonment
entries.body: Three GitHub workflows were reported as dead weight on last-run date (dormant 2-4 months) and approved for retirement. Reading their triggers first: two were GitHub Pages deploys on paths:[landing/**] serving LIVE public sites on Caleb's own domains (drug-cash.calebdunn.tech, dg.calebdunn.tech), one was a tags:v* release pipeline to the private registry, one a tags:v* ghcr publisher deliberately GitHub-only. Silence was correct behaviour. Read the trigger, not the timestamp. Second lesson: an approval is for the thing DESCRIBED — when the description turns out false the approval does not transfer, so re-ask.

entries.title: A comment asserting 'all callers do X' ages silently
entries.body: Migration 0016 adds users.show_uptime_display NOT NULL then DROP DEFAULT, justified by 'CreateUser always supplies it'. True of storage.go CreateUser, false of internal/storage/seed_demo.go — the one INSERT INTO users in the tree that is not CreateUser. It produced SQLSTATE 23502 inside a log.Fatalf, which on an ephemeral demo sidecar would have killed the container on EVERY cold start. Enforce the invariant (keep the DEFAULT, a trigger, or a single write path) rather than asserting it in prose.

entries.title: A QA brief must assert the SHA, not the version
entries.body: Only a release PR bumps package.json, so on a feature or docs PR the branch reports the SAME version as prod and 'confirm /version.json matches this PR' green-lights a staging box running literally anything. The identity assertion must name the artifact, not a label that travels with it — same rule as pinning a promotion digest, since homepad:<sha>-beta and homepad:<semver> are different builds of the same source.

entries.title: Playwright's --hide-scrollbars blinds width gates to classic scrollbars
entries.body: The #428 gate passed at 375px on macOS and in the CI image while QA measured unequal segments: Playwright launches Chromium with --hide-scrollbars, so the group was 303px; in QA's browser the page and modal-body scrollbars took 15px each (273px). Width-sensitive gate specs should use test.use({launchOptions:{ignoreDefaultArgs:['--hide-scrollbars']}}) and add a case with styled ::-webkit-scrollbar plus overflow-y:scroll on the scroll containers. Reproduce QA's numbers before fixing.

entries.title: Cycle 1 complete: two releases, 16 issues, 16.7.1 in production in two days
entries.body: Metrics: 2026-10-11 → 2026-10-12; 6 work items (A,D,B,C,E,F) all DONE in the planned serial order; 7 PRs; 16 issues closed with evidence; one QA block (#518), fixed in-PR. Worked: strict serialization through the staging slot (no overwritten builds); negative controls on every new guard; verifying rollouts from the log line and prod from /version.json at prod. Harder: sizing (#428 and #367 were not quick wins); a stale background watcher was misread as #516 merging, corrected before acting on it; handoff/cycle log were written once at close-out rather than after each merge, as the plan required. Next cycle: update the log at each merge; give promotion requests the staging-release -beta digest of the tagged commit, not the one prod-release prints.

entries.title: Cycle 2 complete: the agent work took a day, and the evidence it needed took another 8 hours
entries.body: Metrics: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-13. Items A, A2, B, C, E all merged in serial order (6 PRs, every one single-reviewer; the duplicate-QA pattern did not recur). Released 16.7.2 (not promoted). Closed #452 #455 #423 #487 #524 #507 #414 #528. Filed #529 and homepad-api#72. Worked: simulating the pod (a node image plus a CDP sidecar, starved with --cpus=0.35) reproduced #524 before QA could; negative controls guarded against a stale dist/; the cycle log was updated per merge. Harder: the cycle's close depended on evidence that only exists in the cluster or a QA pod, and the one route to it (Joe) silently dropped messages for ~8h. Gitea auto-closed #455 and #507 from squash titles with no evidence; both were reopened. Next: in a PR title use 'Refs #N' when the closing evidence is a separate run; anchor routed asks on the issue itself.

entries.title: A Remote Control send that says 'delivered' proves nothing; anchor routed asks on the issue
entries.body: SendMessage to a Remote Control session returns success and reports nothing back. On 2026-10-12, four sends to joe_tmux_1 never reached Joe and two of his never reached me. The fourth send's result noted the name now pointed at a NEW session (restarted); Joe answered every issue within minutes of that send. How to apply: (1) put the full ask on the Gitea issue first and make the message a pointer to it; (2) when a send result says 'new session under a previously used name', resend everything, since the new session has no prior context; (3) treat silence past ~1h as a delivery failure, not a refusal, and tell the user so they can check the session directly.

entries.title: A safety guard in one helper doesn't protect a package that bypasses the helper
entries.body: homepad-api #67 guarded internal/testsupport against truncating a non-test database after the 2026-09-13 prod wipe. internal/storage's tests open the database through their own requireDatabaseURL, which has no guard, and they TRUNCATE users/categories CASCADE and DROP COLUMN. The guard exists, and the gap shipped beside it. Evidence it bites: stg-Test* users in the staging DB. How to apply: put a destructive-operation guard at the single choke point every path must go through (the DSN accessor), and test that the choke point is the only way in (see the 'all callers do X' memory).

entries.title: curl -H @- and -d @- both read stdin; only one can
entries.body: Piping the auth header via `-H @-` and the JSON body via `-d @-` in the same curl gives Gitea an empty or garbled body, and every call 422s (nothing posted, nothing closed). How to apply: the header takes stdin, the body goes in a file (`-d @file`), written with a quoted heredoc or from Python.

entries.title: A time-gated next step needs a scheduled trigger, or it stalls until Caleb asks
entries.body: The 24h staging soak for homepad-api #81 ended 2026-10-27 21:18Z, but Phase 2 didn't start until Caleb asked on 10-29: two days lost. Caleb's retro feedback (collab 7.0): 'I have to follow up too often'. How to apply: whenever a step waits on time (a soak, a QA turnaround, a date), schedule a check-in for when the wait ends (CronCreate or ScheduleWakeup in the session), and act on it without waiting to be asked. Never end a turn with 'I'll do X when Y' unless something will actually wake me when Y happens.

entries.title: Unblock dependencies on other agents early: escalate on a clock, or route around them
entries.body: Caleb: 'better follow up to completion and interaction with other agents, or solutions to work around needing other agents.' Evidence: a Gitea comment to Joe sat unseen for 14h, and Joe answered 6 minutes after a direct SendMessage ping; #545 (docs-only) waited 4+ days for QA. How to apply: (1) post every Joe request on Gitea AND by SendMessage to joe_tmux_1, together; (2) if there's no reply within 4h, re-ping, and if still none within 24h, tell Caleb with a concrete workaround; (3) don't let a low-value PR block a high-value one (fold a docs row into the next PR instead of waiting); (4) verify state myself where read-only access allows (e.g. staging over http), rather than asking an agent.

entries.title: Staging is http-only; an https 404 is not an outage
entries.body: homepad-staging.10.17.2.213.nip.io is served only on Traefik's web entrypoint. Over https every path returns Traefik's 'no router' 404. I reported staging down and pinged Joe twice; Joe found it healthy. How to apply: probe http:// /version.json (200) and /api/me (401) before calling staging down. CLAUDE.md and .add/config.json listed https:// — corrected.

entries.title: Build work goes to an Opus agent at high effort, with a full brief and side-effect rules
entries.body: Standing rule from Caleb. Kid-accounts phases built this way each passed QA on the first try. The briefs must include: a worktree on a new branch; TDD; no merge or deploy; check git status before every commit (one agent committed a 17 MB binary); don't start or stop Docker or other services (one did, which auto-started unrelated containers). Verify the agent's claims (PR, SHA, CI, diff) before reporting.

entries.title: A growth plan that depends on the owner's posts needs those posts scheduled first, not last
entries.body: Every M7 funnel fix shipped by 10-17, but visitors went 32 → 35 over 17 days, because no launch post went out; the posts can only come from Caleb's accounts. How to apply: in a time-boxed growth goal, put the owner-dependent action on a dated calendar in week 1, and if its date passes, raise it as the top blocker in every update, with a ready-to-paste draft attached.
